title: Completeness of inverse limits of power-torsion sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be any scheme with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ be a finitely generated ideal. Let $\underline A$ be the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A complex $K$ of $\underline A$-module sheaves is called derived $I$-complete if on every slice site and for every local section $f$ of $I\underline A$ on that slice, $R\mathcal Hom(\underline A[1/f],K)=0$, using [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; here $\underline A[1/f]$ is the sheafification of sectionwise localization at $f$ on the slice. The full subcategory of module sheaves that are derived complete as degree-zero complexes is a weak Serre subcategory: in an exact sequence $F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to F_4\to F_5$ with the four outside terms complete, $F_3$ is complete. It is closed under inverse limits of countable inverse sequences. Every module sheaf killed by $I^n$ for some $n\geq1$ belongs to it. Consequently every sheaf locally of the form $\varprojlim_n F_n$ with $I^nF_n=0$ is derived complete; every bounded cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with such terms is derived complete as well. All categories of module sheaves and derived categories are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $X$, no section-finiteness and no surjectivity of the transition maps are assumed.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), clauses (1), (4), (5), on the pro-etale site; power-torsion objects and completeness are described immediately before the proposition in Section Tag 099P (section-derived-completion-proetale). Bounded-complex consequence by finite kernels and cokernels, and locality from the slice definition.

proof.text: Use the pro-etale multiplication-difference criterion to characterize degree-zero completeness on every slice and every local ideal section. The derived restriction/single-complex comparison and the regular-module localization colimit identify this with the existing completeness predicates.

Restrict the exact five-term row by the exact module restriction functor. Apply exact countable powers and their natural difference; Mathlib's abelian five lemma gives invertibility of the middle difference from the outside four. Apply the criterion.

Module restriction is a right adjoint by its explicit adjunction, hence preserves inverse limits. Countable powers also preserve these limits. Naturality makes the limit of invertible difference components invertible; conjugate by the restriction/limit comparison and apply the criterion. No transition is assumed epic.

For a section f in the extended ideal, the extended-ideal power theorem puts f^n in extended I^n on every further slice. Annihilation gives nilpotence of section multiplication. The power of the countable product shift has coordinate projection equal to projection j+n followed by multiplication by f^n. Hence the shift is nilpotent, and one minus this shift is invertible by the finite geometric series. Apply the criterion.

Convert the existing ringed-site complete-element predicate to the same difference criterion, comparing its representative-based restriction with exact derived restriction and its telescope localization with genuine sectionwise localization. Covering-sieve descent of complete elements then applies. On each covering member use the given limit presentation, preservation of the limit by powers, and the nilpotence argument for each G_n.

Each complex term is complete by the preceding local power-torsion limit argument. After restriction, the difference is therefore invertible in every degree. The complex clause of the criterion gives local RHom vanishing for Q of the restricted complex. The exact derived-restriction factorization transfers it to the restriction of QK. This argument also works without boundedness.

proof_origin.place: Tags 099P and 099Q: implemented five-term, ordinary-limit, nilpotence, locality and termwise arguments, together with the multiplication-difference criterion, in Lean.

lean.statement: theorem torsionLimitSheaf_completeness (X : Scheme.{t}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (_hI : I.FG) : (∀ (F₁ F₂ F₃ F₄ F₅ : TorsionCompletionModules X A) (a : F₁ ⟶ F₂) (b : F₂ ⟶ F₃) (c : F₃ ⟶ F₄) (d : F₄ ⟶ F₅) (hab : a ≫ b = 0) (hbc : b ≫ c = 0) (hcd : c ≫ d = 0), (ShortComplex.mk a b hab).Exact → (ShortComplex.mk b c hbc).Exact → (ShortComplex.mk c d hcd).Exact → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F₁ → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F₂ → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F₄ → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F₅ → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F₃) ∧ (∀ (F : ℕ → TorsionCompletionModules X A) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, F (n + 1) ⟶ F n), (∀ n : ℕ, IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I (F n)) → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I (limit (Functor.ofOpSequence f))) ∧ (∀ (F : TorsionCompletionModules X A) (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → IsAnnihilatedByModuleIdeal (torsionCompletionModuleRing X A) (torsionCompletionIdeal X (I ^ n)) (torsionCompletionIdealInclusion X (I ^ n)) F → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F) ∧ (∀ F : TorsionCompletionModules X A, IsLocallyPowerTorsionLimit X I F → IsTorsionCompletionCompleteSheaf X I F) ∧ (∀ K : CochainComplex (TorsionCompletionModules X A) ℤ, (∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (K.X i)) → (∀ i : ℤ, IsLocallyPowerTorsionLimit X I (K.X i)) → IsTorsionCompletionComplete X I ((torsionCompletionLocalization X A).obj K))
